title: Hemangiol (propranolol) oral solution: summary of product characteristics, EPAR product information
authors: European Medicines Agency, Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use
journal: European Medicines Agency; marketing authorisation EU/1/14/919/001, first authorised 23 April 2014, renewed 15 January 2019; product information document of 12 June 2026
funder: not stated; EU product information carries no funding statement.
result: Propranolol for proliferating infantile haemangioma requiring systemic therapy, initiated in infants aged 5 weeks to 5 months and given for 6 months. Contraindicated in asthma or history of bronchospasm, second- or third-degree AV block, sinus node disease, bradycardia or hypotension below age-specific limits, cardiogenic shock, uncontrolled heart failure, Prinzmetal's angina, severe peripheral arterial disturbance including Raynaud's phenomenon, infants prone to hypoglycaemia and phaeochromocytoma. Propranolol prevents the catecholamine response that corrects hypoglycaemia and masks its adrenergic signs; it can aggravate hypoglycaemia in children during fasting, infection or vomiting, and episodes may present as seizures or coma; the risk remains throughout treatment, and corticosteroids may increase it. Lower respiratory infection with wheeze requires temporary stopping, and isolated bronchospasm permanent stopping. In three clinical studies of 435 infants, very common adverse reactions were sleep disorders (16.7%), aggravated respiratory tract infections such as bronchitis and bronchiolitis, diarrhoea (16.5%) and vomiting (11.5%); hypoglycaemic seizure, hypotension, Raynaud's phenomenon, agranulocytosis and hyperkalaemia in large ulcerated haemangioma are listed from compassionate use and the literature. Overdose may cause bradycardia, hypotension, AV block, heart failure, bronchospasm, hypoglycaemia and, because propranolol crosses the blood-brain barrier, seizures.
